title: Strava Weekly Distance vs Goal
dataSources: Strava API activities (`strava:activity`), Garmin Connect (`garmin:activity`), Fitbit Web API (`fitbit:activity`), Peloton workout history (`peloton:workout`).
app: Strava / Garmin Connect / Fitbit / Peloton / Zwift APIs and webhooks via Splunk HEC scripted inputs; GPX/FIT/CSV activity exports ingested as file inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity type=Run
| bin _time span=1w
| stats sum(distance_km) as km, sum(moving_time_s) as secs by _time
| eval goal_km=40, pct_of_goal=round(100*km/goal_km,1)
| eval status=if(km>=goal_km,"goal met","behind")
| sort - _time
description: Sums your Strava running distance per calendar week and compares it to a personal weekly goal so you can see, at a glance, whether you are on track.
value: Turns a vague sense of 'am I running enough?' into a concrete weekly number against a target, which is far more motivating than staring at individual activities.
implementation: Pull activities from the Strava API into `index=personal` on a schedule (or via Strava webhooks); adjust `goal_km` to your target and alert yourself on a Sunday if you are behind.
visualization: Column chart of weekly kilometres with a goal reference line and percent-of-goal label.
grandmaExplanation: It adds up how far you ran each week and tells you if you have hit your target, so you know whether to squeeze in one more run.
